verdict.rationale: ImageMagick's own site claims API bindings for C, C++, Python, .NET and Node.js, and its llms.txt says developers can integrate it into applications, so first-party client libraries for mainstream languages are documented. The evidence is a single one-line claim and does not show whether these bindings are vendor-maintained or versioned. Missing for 10: evidence the bindings are vendor-maintained rather than third-party, versioning/release cadence for the bindings, per-language documentation depth, independent or hands-on corroboration.
